target_customer: University students who use a campus feed for anonymous posts and stories
problem: Students wanted a private, campus only place to share thoughts and funny stories; Chillabit offered a live feed for the university community.
business_model: Free consumer social app with no revenue model described in sources

founders.name: Kyle Kaiser
education: University of Alberta student or alumnus (per UAlberta Folio, 2016-02)

founders.name: Tamara Bain
education: University of Alberta student or alumna (per UAlberta Folio, 2016-02)

founders.name: Mark Galloway
education: University of Alberta student or alumnus (per UAlberta Folio, 2016-02)

founders.name: Benjamin Lavin
education: University of Alberta student or alumnus (per UAlberta Folio, 2016-02)

founders.name: Sabby Choudhary
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Sabby Choudhary; UAlberta Folio names Anmol Choudhary, possibly the same person, so the name is unconfirmed.

exit.reason: Announced after four years of operation; reason not given in the source.

competitors.name: Yik Yak
competitors.what: Location based anonymous message board popular on college campuses, the app Chitter was compared with

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile feed with university email sign up, voting and moderation is standard app work for a student team.

defensibility.rationale: Campus by campus network effects exist, but Yik Yak style rivals and later apps like Fizz and Sidechat show easy replication.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent absorbing Chillabit; the app shut down in 2019.

market_need_then: The UAlberta Folio (2016-02) reported more than 20,000 users on five Canadian campuses for the predecessor Chitter, and Yik Yak had shown student demand for anonymous campus apps.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual tone; YC one liner calls it the best way to procrastinate.

branding.community_and_virality: A university newspaper ran a streeter about the shutdown, which shows campus awareness.

brand_strength.rationale: Student press knew the app, but no mascot, merch or lasting community evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: The app launched as Chitter at the University of Alberta in September 2015, reached about 20,000 users on five campuses by early 2016, joined YC in Winter 2016 and announced its shutdown in March 2019 after four years of operation. No source states why, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. Anonymous campus apps faced strong rivals, but that is context not a sourced cause.
notes: The funding rounds rest on a single database (Seedtable) via a search summary; the page itself returned 403. Seedtable says $1M seed and $880K venture round dated March 2016; CB Insights lists only Y Combinator. The shutdown article is from The Gateway (April 2019) and describes a company founded as Chitter; linking it to this Chillabit rests on the matching name and founder names in the UAlberta Folio. The company website safety check was rate limited so chillabit.io was not read. YC lists team size 3 but five founder profiles. Headquarters differ across sources (San Francisco, Palo Alto, Kitchener).
